Hi Julia — thanks for the clear list. I'm attaching a consolidated draft (Redwood-SIG-BCDR-answers-v1.pdf) that covers our current answers; Rishi and Mina are looped in to add technical specifics and evidence references. Quick highlights here:

- RTO targets: Hosted API standard endpoints: 300s (5 min) for 99th pct under normal load; Dedicated reserved capacity endpoints: 120s (2 min) for 99th pct.
- RPO targets: Nearline replication for customer-requested data: 1 hour; critical metadata and logs: 15 minutes.
- Backups: Full snapshot weekly; incremental snapshots every 6 hours. Customer data stored in encrypted object storage; snapshots retained 90 days by default, 1 year on request for enterprise contracts.
- Regional replication: Primary/secondary in two regions per customer where available (US-EAST and US-WEST by default). Failover policy: automatic routing to secondary region via our control plane with health checks; automatic fallback to compatible model variant if the primary model is unavailable.

Attachments: Redwood-SIG-BCDR-answers-v1.pdf (draft), k8s-backup-policy-2025.pdf (policy excerpt). We don't include full runbooks in this draft; Mina will add a summary of the last DR test and provide a sanitized runbook snippet or a Drive link.

Let us know if you'd prefer a DocuSign or shared Drive package for evidence.

Julia / Marissa — adding technical clarifications to the draft answers:

- RTO/RPO by service:
  * Hosted API (multi-tenant): RTO 300s (we measure 99th% rolling); RPO ~1 hour for embeddings/service-level customer objects. Critical control-plane metadata: RPO 15 minutes due to continuous replication to hot storage.
  * Dedicated (customer single-tenant cluster): RTO 120s under normal operating conditions; RPO configurable down to 15 minutes for enterprise customers via enhanced replication.

- Backups and consistency:
  * Backups are application-consistent for metadata and KV stores via snapshotting and leader-fenced checkpoints. Object storage snapshots include manifest files for fast rehydration.
  * Off-site replication: encrypted snapshots are replicated to a secondary cloud region within 30 minutes of creation; cross-region replication is asynchronous but sequenced to preserve consistency for control-plane objects.

- Failover process:
  * Automatic health checks trigger traffic reroute through smart routing. For stateful workloads we accelerate recovery by mounting the most recent snapshot in read-write mode and replaying WAL segments (where applicable).
  * Manual escalation: if automated failover doesn't restore service within SLA window, operations run the documented runbook (link below) and open a priority incident with customer engineering.

- DR test evidence: last full failover drill for multi-region hosted tier executed 2025-11-02; all critical services failed over within RTO targets. We can provide a sanitized playbook excerpt and a redacted incident report.

I'll upload the runbook excerpt and sanitized incident report to the Drive folder and share a link.

— Rishi
